sources.source: Statistics on so called honour-based abuse offences, England and Wales, year ending March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The official release records 2,949 honour-based-abuse-related offences and 2,047 related incidents in the year ending March 2025. It states that the figures likely represent only a fraction of actual abuse and that Metropolitan Police recording-system changes affected the latest comparison.
sources.quality_effect: Adds hidden-crime context with offence-versus-incident, under-reporting, police-identification, low-volume force-area and recording-system guards; recorded cases are not prevalence or parcel risk.

sources.source: Sexual offences in England and Wales overview: year ending March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The accredited release estimates that 1.9% of people aged 16 years and over, around 900,000 people, experienced sexual assault including attempts. Police recorded 209,079 sexual offences, with part of the increase linked to two new Online Safety Act offences.
sources.quality_effect: Adds victimisation context while separating survey prevalence from police demand, retaining half-sample uncertainty, age-band comparability, reporting change, recording practice and legislation-version guards.

sources.source: Domestic abuse prevalence and trends, England and Wales: year ending March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The accredited release estimates that 7.8% of people aged 16 years and over, around 3.8 million people, experienced domestic abuse in the last year. Police recorded 1,350,460 domestic-abuse-related incidents and crimes, including 816,493 crimes.
sources.quality_effect: Adds domestic-abuse context with new-question-set, pre-2024 non-comparability, survey-versus-police, incident-versus-crime, disclosure and recording-practice guards.

sources.source: Stalking: findings from the Crime Survey for England and Wales, year ending March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The accredited CSEW release estimates that 2.9% of people aged 16 years and over, around 1.4 million people, experienced stalking in the last year. Related CSEW reporting estimates that 8.6%, around 4.2 million people, experienced harassment.
sources.quality_effect: Adds stalking and harassment context with self-completion, age-range, repeated-behaviour definition, one-off harassment, half-sample and police-counting-rule guards.

sources.source: Police complaints statistics for England and Wales report - 2024/25
sources.verified_fact: The official report records 94,940 complaints logged by 43 police forces and 91,750 complaints finalised in 2024/25. The IOPC states that improved complaint handling and recording can increase logged volumes and that the statistics remain experimental.
sources.quality_effect: Adds accountability-system context with complaint-versus-allegation, informal-versus-formal handling, force-practice, experimental-statistics and access-to-system guards; complaint volume is not crime prevalence.

sources.source: Crime against businesses: findings from the 2023 Commercial Victimisation Survey
sources.verified_fact: The official survey estimates that 26% of business premises, around 409,000 premises, experienced a measured crime in the previous 12 months; prevalence was 41% in wholesale and retail. The release was corrected in September 2024.
sources.quality_effect: Adds business-safety context with premises-versus-enterprise, sector coverage, survey uncertainty, repeat victimisation, fraud undercount, correction and only-two-years-all-sector guards.

sources.source: Abuse during childhood in England and Wales: March 2024
sources.verified_fact: The official-statistics-in-development release estimates that 29.0% of adults, around 13.6 million people, experienced emotional, physical or sexual abuse or neglect before age 18. It states that redeveloped questions and population coverage prevent comparison with earlier publications.
sources.quality_effect: Adds safeguarding context with retrospective-adult, overlapping-category, disclosure, current-characteristic, redeveloped-question and non-current-prevalence guards.

sources.source: Nature of crime tables England and Wales: year ending March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The accredited 26 March 2026 release provides CSEW incident-detail datasets covering timing, location, offender information, victim perceptions, injuries, weapons and losses across violence, robbery, burglary, theft, criminal damage, fraud and computer misuse.
sources.quality_effect: Adds incident-characteristic crosschecks while retaining survey-sample, recall, victim-perception, household-population, offence-specific denominator and 2021-to-2022 telephone-survey modality guards.
